# Private Next ESLint plugin fork

This is a private fork of the official `@next/eslint-plugin-next@16.3.6` npm package, published by Vercel under the MIT license. It is identified as `16.3.6-apollo.2`; it is not an upstream release. The upstream tarball is `https://registry.npmjs.org/@next/eslint-plugin-next/-/eslint-plugin-next-16.3.6.tgz`, with SHA-256 `63e351657611f090d7dfacfde30d60cc3c5f9cd046287f98b4fc36fa25fb74a5` and npm integrity `sha512-jowwDX+7DOlDIjJLgTMxudw+k37QnWu1JkZLkSi9MaJBfDYcfhAPMKBhXL0idYzFN/AGg//axnOR4cLkHX/Rng==`. The original bytes of all 56 package files are recorded in `UPSTREAM_SHA256.json`; `PATCH.diff` shows the complete source and metadata delta.

The disposable W27/W28 run stopped at `security-audit` with exit 1; its filtered output did not identify the precise finding. A local audit of the same commit reported the `braces` advisory [GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm). The pinned upstream Next plugin pulled `fast-glob` and that vulnerable dependency chain; the Tailwind 3 toolchain carried another affected chain. Official compatible releases did not remove both chains at this checkpoint. Tailwind was upgraded to 4.3.3 with `@tailwindcss/postcss@4.3.3`, while this fork changes only the plugin's directory glob helper and package metadata.

Only `dist/utils/get-root-dirs.js` changes runtime behavior. This second fork revision replaces `fast-glob@3.3.1` with `glob@13.0.6` (`sha512-Wjlyrolmm8uDpm/ogGyXZXb1Z+Ca2B8NbJwqBVg0axK9GbBeoS7yGV6vjXnYdGm6X53iehEuxxbyiKp8QmN4Vw==`). The first private revision used `tinyglobby@0.2.17`, but Linux CI showed it omitted symbolic-link directory roots that upstream returned. The helper now follows links, keeps only directories, normalizes Windows separators, and prevents terminal literal globstars from returning their base directory. Tests cover real Linux symlinks and Windows junctions; wildcard result order is not treated as an API contract. Every rule file, declaration, and ESLint configuration remains byte-identical to upstream and is checked by `tests/ops/vendor-eslint-plugin-next.test.mjs`.

The upstream `dist/utils/node-attributes.js` has a trailing space on line 2. `.gitattributes` disables only the `blank-at-eol` check for that exact path so its byte-for-byte provenance remains valid; the upstream hash test still checks it. Other whitespace checks and all other code paths retain their existing rules.

The fork metadata sets `private: true`, drops upstream build scripts and development dependencies because the official compiled `dist` is vendored, and declares `eslint >=9` as a peer. The application pins ESLint 9. The exact package is packed to `../next-eslint-plugin-next-16.3.6-apollo.2.tgz` and selected through the root package's direct dependency and exact-name npm override; the lockfile binds that tarball by SHA-512 integrity. The packaged tarball is required by Docker before `npm ci`. The license is copied from the Next.js `v16.3.6` source tag (`https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/v16.3.6/license.md`), SHA-256 `ee765244e2d59f5234d474f62e0766fa0c8b99af967fdd4c0cb8dcb0c76ea224`.

For maintenance, compare a new official release's `get-root-dirs` and dependencies with this patch, then remove the fork if upstream eliminates the vulnerable chain without changing rule behavior. Repack only after updating the source manifest and tests. Do not publish this package as an upstream version or replace the audit with a waiver.
